ruleName: Ball moves after being put back
title: What happens if the ball rolls away after being replaced?
question: After you have marked, lifted, and replaced your ball on the green, it suddenly rolls away on its own before you take your putt. What should you do?

choices.text: Play the ball from its new position
Replace the ball on its original spot with no penalty
Take a penalty stroke and put it back
Start the hole over from the tee

explanation: If the ball moves on its own after being replaced, you must put it back on its original spot with no penalty.

juniorVersion.title: If Your Ball Rolls Away After You Put It Back
juniorVersion.question: You mark your ball on the green, pick it up, and put it back. Before you hit your putt, the ball rolls away by itself. What should you do?

choices.text: Play the ball from where it stopped
Put the ball back where it was with no penalty
Add a penalty and put it back
Go back and start the hole again

juniorVersion.explanation: If your ball moves by itself after you put it back on the green, you need to put it back where it was before. You do not get a penalty.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: The short, smooth grass around the hole where you putt.
Extra shots added to your score if you break a rule.
Put a small coin or marker behind your ball so you can pick it up and then put it back.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Show kids how the wind or slope can sometimes make a ball move by itself on the green, and why it's important to know what to do if this happens.
likelyMisconceptions: Kids might think they always have to play the ball from where it stops.
Some may think you always get a penalty when your ball moves.
